newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end lower, following Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end lower, following Wall Street.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed sharply lower after Wall Street's weakness paved the way for a much-expected correction in prices, brokers said.

The Bovespa index of the 49 most active shares fell 874 points or 1.11 percent to 78,175 points. Market turnover was a moderate 490.8 million reais ($471.9 million) as capital inflows slowed in part because of the 0.2 percent CPMF tax on financial transactions, which will take effect Thursday, traders said.
They said it was natural that liquidity would drop somewhat since local and foreign investors now have to take into account the new tax.

Benchmark Telebras and oil state firm Petrobras preferred stocks led the market's fall. Telebras preferred dropped 1.21 percent to end at 89.60 reais, while Petrobras non-voting stock fell 2.84 percent to 188 reais.
The preferred shares of state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce lost 1.62 percent to 24.25 reais following the behavior of other top blue-chips.
Although news that the start of Vale's privatization would be postponed until April appeared to be negative to the stock, analysts did not attribute the share weakness to the delay.
"We found that Vale's selloff in the first quarter was unlikely," one trader said.
The power sector index comprising the nine most liquid stocks of the electrical sector, fell 0.57 percent to close at 2,273 percent.
Despite today's drop, observers think the market's uptrend remains. "The market is likely to recover tomorrow. A correction is healthy," one analyst said.
